summary: Fix review findings DR-03, DR-04, DR-08, DR-11, DR-14 and DR-16 in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs: browser updates of one room go to the store as one transaction per batch (lookahead group commit over the room's recorded update classes, 50 ms linger cut short by a durability waiter, one row per update, about 3 round trips per batch) on a new store.Pool.RoomAppends() pool of 8; a new dispatch_doc_head notification channel ({r,v,p}) sent beside the bare-id dispatch_doc_changed, whose handler makes no query for a process's own writes or for a room already at v; an in-memory head tracker (generations, own-write in-flight counts via store.AfterCommit, epoch per LISTEN connection) that answers coldRead's cache-hit check and takePreload's head check without a database read; signalled settlement waits; one issue read and one requestActor per socket open with counters instead of scans; update classes without copies; preloads released at once; a read budget derived from the Go memory limit; dispatch_rooms on /debug/vars; and browser-editor workload, wire-level round-trip counter, room-connection sampler and update latency added to INFRA-589's harness for the before/after runs.

agreements.what: Whole-markdown-per-version measured at 1x and 10x, a storage-format change if needed is a new INFRA-514 child; cross-pod read freshness bounded by notification delivery accepted with the two-Service p99 measured; editor rates 20 x 2/s at 1x and 200 x 2/s at 10x plus both over the 0.25x REST mix; no order with INFRA-179, documentReadBudget works without a Go memory limit and follows INFRA-179's once it lands.

dispatch_doc_changed not changed in place; new channel sent beside it, listen on the new one; INFRA-556 owns gate semantics, INFRA-605 calls one agreed gate function; one process id; one head tracker that INFRA-556 D8 uses; connectionState shared for socket admission.

queueAppendGate(b *pgx.Batch, room string, through int64, kind appendKind) *appendGate, (g *appendGate) head() (int64, error), gateAppend(ctx, tx, room, through, kind); processID via uuid.NewString() in docs.New with Service.ProcessID() string; channel dispatch_doc_head JSON {r,v,p} from every content-changing write, compaction none; head tracker observe/connected/disconnected/head. Hub with Handle(channel, func(payload string)) built by INFRA-556; INFRA-605 registers there or, if first, on the stale-room evictor's existing connection.

INFRA-593 owns fold.go, Load, LoadDocument, compaction and LoadDoc's second decode, and moves the load's CPU after commit (DR-08 part b); row model, headVersion and DocumentStamp unchanged, compaction never rewrites the head row; INFRA-605 calls s.noteStoredUpdates(room, head, oldest) once per committed batch.

Harness at packages/envoy/loadtest (Go main loadgen inside the envoy module); INFRA-605 adds the editors workload, the proxy round-trip counter, the sampler column and latency tables in its own files and sections.

Per-pool application_name dispatch-<pool> (dispatch-rooms, dispatch-room-appends); RoomAppends acquire bounded at 30 s by INFRA-592's tracer; settleRoomWithin and store/pool.go rebase on whichever merges second; RoomAppends goes in the AGENTS.md pool budget table.
One LISTEN connection per process for new channels through pglisten.Hub; INFRA-605 needs only payload handlers (PID request withdrawn).

findings.finding: A version-only head tracker serves stale cache hits after a prune and re-append; compaction changes the stamp's xmin.
findings.answer: The tracker keeps per-document generations from one process-wide counter, not versions; a cache entry keeps the token taken before its fold and is served without a database read only while the generation and epoch are unchanged and no own write is in flight; a prune notifies (dispatch_doc_head with the lower head); INFRA-593 confirmed compaction never rewrites the head row and it sends nothing. Test TestACachedColdReadNeedsNoDatabaseReadWhileTheTrackerTrustsIt does the prune-to-N-2 and append-back case on a second Service.

findings.finding: A notification-fed tracker lags commits on another pod, which conflicts with 'reads never older than the store'.
findings.answer: INFRA-514's architect accepted freshness bounded by notification delivery (04:37Z), with the store read while LISTEN is down; a two-Service test prints the p99. Own writes bump synchronously after commit through store.AfterCommit, so a process reads its own writes; the evictor's slow locked confirmation moves to a per-room goroutine so tracker updates never queue behind it.

findings.finding: The lookahead batch over the room's update FIFO can cross suppression slots, other room instances and persistCh order.
findings.answer: Batch rules in plan D1.2: the longest prefix from the queue's oldest entry with the same cursor instance as u, no queued suppression slot, each update decoding alone, holding u, capped at 256 updates and 1 MiB; otherwise u alone as today. Versions follow the room's commit order. Race test TestABatchStopsAtASuppressedUpdateAndAtAnotherRoomInstance, 200 iterations.

findings.finding: Per-update outcomes on a failed batch, late ygo calls after a failed-room handover, credits and counters are undefined.
findings.answer: Stored classes carry a stored mark that travels through handOverFailedRoomLocked; durableAppends finishes on the counting record at commit; pendingUpdates ends at ygo's late call; a refused gate or failed commit stores and marks nothing and each other update meets today's failed-room path; credits land after commit and before unlock. Test TestAGateRefusalOrFailedCommitStoresNothingOfTheBatchAndEachUpdateEndsOnce.

findings.finding: Batched owed and pending-author writes must keep per-version meaning.
findings.answer: One doc_pending_authors row per credited update at its version; last_actor is the last credited update's actor when it names one. Test TestABatchLeavesThePendingAuthorRowsOneAtATimeAppendsLeave compares with one-at-a-time appends.

findings.finding: A new VersionedStore method would bypass the test wrappers; the in-transaction append path needs the same SQL.
findings.answer: AppendUpdatesWithCredit replaces AppendUpdateWithCredit and every wrapper moves to it (listed in D1.3); one implementation of gate, insert, notify, owed and authors serves both paths.

findings.finding: Ordering and shared APIs with INFRA-556 are not settled.
findings.answer: Settled over Envoy with INFRA-63's architect (04:17Z) and INFRA-556's implementer (04:34Z, 04:39Z): gate function, process id, channel and payload, head tracker, Hub registration; whichever merges second rebases.

findings.finding: DR-04's roll compatibility needs a pglisten PID change; skipping by process alone is unsafe.
findings.answer: No PID: by INFRA-63's architect's rule rooms follow only dispatch_doc_head; dispatch_doc_changed only invalidates the tracker entry, so an old build's write still invalidates cached reads. Own notifications skip the query only when the cursor equals v or an own write's cursor advance is still pending (then re-checked with no query); a finished own write that left a room behind takes today's decision. Test with an old-channel-only sender.

findings.finding: The new pool is missed by the drain, the docs and the wait-for argument; Compact on the same pool would starve appends.
findings.answer: Only the browser batch uses RoomAppends; other withRoomLock callers stay; INFRA-593 moves compaction to its own pool; Use() and the drain count it; HoldsConnection kept; running-dispatch.md, AGENTS.md and README updated with the new total (89).

findings.finding: DR-11 details: lock_timeout scope, handover of the idle signal, re-arm cancellation.
findings.answer: Savepoint plus set_config('lock_timeout','100ms',true) restored after the lock; the idle channel moves with the counts and waiters re-resolve the record; the re-arm goes through scheduleSettleAfterLocked so settleWG and stopAllSettleTimers cover it.

findings.finding: DR-14: validateUpdate claim wrong; auth-frame and carried reads can be stale; verdict must track updates; counters across handover; overlap with INFRA-179.
findings.answer: Validate item dropped (INFRA-593 removes that decode); ServeHTTP's read is recorded on the room state and authorize treats either closed view as closed (test with a close during loadTree); the outside-schema verdict is kept by the replica observer; counters are service-wide; INFRA-179 order: the later rebases (architect, 04:37Z).

findings.finding: DR-16 limits have no inputs on main and collide with INFRA-179; RLIMIT_NOFILE is useless as an input.
findings.answer: readBudget = GOMEMLIMIT/16 clamped to 64 MiB..1 GiB, 256 MiB with no limit (works before and after INFRA-179); room and connection caps become settings DISPATCH_MAX_LIVE_ROOMS and DISPATCH_MAX_DOC_CONNECTIONS; RLIMIT_NOFILE not used; identity match keeps the byte comparison as fallback, with a test.

findings.finding: The three before/after metrics must be measured the same way on both builds; 10x on main collapses; editor workload details.
findings.answer: Round trips counted by the proxy from the Postgres wire protocol (Sync and Query per connection, statement text from Parse), room work by statement pattern; connections held by rooms from pg_locks advisory holders and waiters plus doc_updates readers; latency as relay and durable (marker probe); editor steps over the 0.25x REST mix isolate the room path and the 10x full-mix before is reported as measured (architect, 04:37Z); sockets use schema_version and Proof-valid edits.

findings.finding: 'Appended in batches' can be read as a merge window or as group commit.
findings.answer: One row per update in one transaction per batch with a 50 ms linger cut short by a durability waiter; recorded as a departure from the review's 100-250 ms merge; the harness's batch-size histogram shows batching per step.
